column3: The Hebrew calls Solomon young and tender; BSB uses young and inexperienced.
The Hebrew repeats each material without naming articles after gold; BSB supplies gold articles.
The Hebrew describes the gift with a completed giving verb and calls the building the holy house; BSB says I now give and uses holy temple.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew pictures consecration as filling one’s hand and the craftsmen’s work as in their hand; BSB uses consecrating himself and work done by craftsmen.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew simply says stones and describes Jehiel’s care through his hand; BSB specifies precious stones and uses under his care.
The Hebrew leaves those responding willingly unnamed and repeats rejoicing as verb and noun for David; BSB identifies the leaders and says David rejoiced greatly.
The Hebrew repeats David’s name before the speech; BSB leaves that second subject implicit.
The Hebrew names victory and describes God reflexively as raising Himself to be head over all; BSB uses splendor and the passive You are exalted.
The Hebrew twice uses Your hand in the singular; BSB combines this as plural Your hands.
The Hebrew speaks of the name of Your glory; BSB uses Your glorious name.

The Hebrew says keep this without an explicit desire noun and uses singular heart for the people’s heart; BSB supplies this desire and uses plural hearts.
The Hebrew calls the commandments, testimonies, and statutes Yours and separately says to do everything; BSB combines keeping and carrying out all Your commandments, decrees, and statutes.
The Hebrew directly commands the assembly to bless the LORD; BSB presents David’s words as Blessed be the LORD.
The Hebrew twice names the LORD as recipient of the sacrifices and burnt offerings; BSB names Him once.
The Hebrew says they anointed Solomon for the LORD; BSB says before the LORD.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the allegiance as giving a hand under Solomon; BSB explicitly calls it pledging allegiance.

The Hebrew says the days of his reign and repeats he reigned for Hebron and Jerusalem; BSB names David and condenses the duration into one sentence.
The Hebrew calls David full of days; BSB uses full of years.
The Hebrew repeatedly uses words or deeds for the accounts; BSB titles them Chronicles.
The Hebrew speaks of the times that passed over David, Israel, and the kingdoms; BSB uses circumstances that came upon them.
